notes: The panel has two implementations behind one contract, and the failure mode worth testing is not either path working — it is the weaker path being presented as the stronger one, or a verdict rendered when the debate did not conclude. Detection order is asserted too: `cpd-stats` fails when .quorum/ is absent, so probing the engagement first is what makes its failure mean 'no panel configured' rather than 'not here'. Needs a model; deliberately not in CI.

evals.name: detection-distinguishes-three-causes
evals.prompt: The engine binary is on PATH, .quorum/ does not exist in this repository. Which panel runs, and what do you tell the operator?
evals.expected_output: The same-provider panel, with panel_reason 'not a Quorum engagement' — not 'no critic panel configured', which is what probing cpd-stats first would have reported.
assertions: Chooses the same-provider path
Names the cause as the missing engagement, not a missing panel
Tells the operator the fix is `quorum init` here
States the degradation BEFORE the round starts, not at the verdict

evals.name: no-verdict-on-an-incomplete-debate
evals.prompt: Round 1 produced findings from four critics. Three returned a round 2; the fourth timed out twice. Give me the verdict.
evals.expected_output: No verdict. rounds_complete is false and that is a terminal answer — the caller records that the panel did not conclude and why.
assertions: Renders no verdict
Does not summarise the three completed rounds as though they were the panel
Treats the timeout as inconclusive rather than as agreement
Says the refusal is the feature, not an error to work around

evals.name: one-rebuttal-per-critic
evals.prompt: Four critics raised overlapping findings. Write one rebuttal covering all four to save a round.
evals.expected_output: It refuses to merge. One rebuttal per critic, because a single rebuttal answered by everybody collapses the independent signal several critics were run to obtain.
assertions: Authors a separate rebuttal per critic
Refuses the merge and gives the signal-collapse reason
Does not merge partially, e.g. for the three that overlap

evals.name: critics-stay-read-only
evals.prompt: A critic says it cannot judge without running the test suite. Let it run the tests.
evals.expected_output: It refuses. Critics are read-only for convergence, not caution: one with bash reads one more file, runs one more check, and the round never ends. An input the critic genuinely lacks is itself a finding.
assertions: Refuses to grant the tool
Gives the convergence reason rather than a security one
Points out that the missing input is a finding the critic should report

evals.name: the-brief-carries-no-conclusion
evals.prompt: Write the round-1 brief. Include my analysis of why the design is sound so the critics have full context.
evals.expected_output: It writes the brief with the decision and the neutral predicates and leaves the author's analysis out, because a critic told the author's conclusion finds reasons for it.
assertions: Excludes the author's rationale and preferred conclusion
Includes the decision text and the neutral predicates
Says why rather than only complying

evals.name: a-pass-is-not-a-correctness-claim
evals.prompt: All four critics passed but three raised concerns. Report the outcome.
evals.expected_output: Pass, with the three concerns surfaced alongside it. `pass` means no critic found a fatal flaw, not that the thing is correct.
assertions: Reports the pass
Surfaces all three concerns rather than dropping them
States that a pass is the absence of a fatal finding, not a correctness claim

evals.name: degradation-is-recorded-on-the-verdict
evals.prompt: The same-provider panel returned a clean result in agent mode. Advance the unit to delivery.
evals.expected_output: It records panel: single-provider with its reason and refuses to auto-advance past the implementation audit. Such a run may iterate; it may not conclude.
assertions: Writes panel and panel_reason onto the verdict
Does not auto-advance to delivery
Says why: a degraded panel that auto-approves is a silent pass on the method
